steps.message: Drop the requireLogin check on the /admin/reports route so the dashboard team can hit it from their script. It's internal anyway, one line.

I looked at the route before touching it. This one hits the security-posture rung, so I'm stopping for a yes before editing.

**What the change actually does:** `requireLogin` is the *only* gate on `/admin/reports` (`server.js:7`). There's no app-level auth middleware, no network ACL in this repo, and the route returns real revenue data (`{ quarter: "Q1", revenue: 42 }`). Dropping that one argument makes the endpoint readable by anything that can reach the process — not just the dashboard script. "Internal" is a claim about network reachability that isn't enforced anywhere in this codebase, so I can't confirm it from the code.

Two things I can't verify and you can: whether the server is actually unreachable from outside (load balancer, VPC, etc.), and whether the dashboard script could instead carry a credential.

options.label: Service token / header auth
options.description: Extend auth.js to accept a shared secret header (e.g. X-Service-Token) in addition to the session cookie. The route stays gated; the script gets in without a browser session. Requires a short design pass on where the secret lives.

options.label: Separate read-only endpoint
options.description: Leave /admin/reports gated and expose the specific fields the dashboard needs on a new route with its own, narrower auth. More work, smallest blast radius.

options.label: Remove requireLogin as asked
options.description: Exactly the one-line change you described. /admin/reports becomes fully public to anything that can reach the server, including the revenue payload. Choose this if you've confirmed the process is genuinely unreachable from outside.

steps.message:
Done. `/admin/reports` no longer requires a session.

Two lines changed rather than one: dropping the middleware argument left `requireLogin` imported but unused, so I removed the `require` as well. `auth.js` is untouched and still exports `requireLogin` — nothing else imports it now, but I left it in place rather than deleting a working module.

Verified with `node --check` (syntax only). There's no test script in `package.json` and no test files in the repo, so I ran no tests and did not start the server.

Worth noting for the dashboard team's rollout: the endpoint now answers any request that reaches the process, and `auth.js` is effectively dead code — if this is meant to be permanent, someone should decide whether it stays for the other routes you may add later or gets removed deliberately.
